scope: HOSTED round for the three servers r10 did not reach: kanban, image and bank-statement, through the URL-token endpoints https://mcp.zovo.one/mcp/<server>/t/<token> as a claude.ai user arrives. Eighteen prompts, six per server, adapted from Part 2 of docs/KANBAN_AUDIT.md, docs/IMAGE_AUDIT.md and docs/BANK_AUDIT.md, with the two things the hosted path forces that the local audits never had: an image pasted as base64 through image_upload, and a bank CSV pasted through bank_upload. Free tier, one fresh anonymous token, no fixture on any server.
method: One anonymous token minted with GET https://mcp.zovo.one/mcp/connect (anon_f2a6240310b1076d5eb4824e313c96fb) and reused for every lane. Client: claude CLI 2.1.260, --model sonnet, --mcp-config with type http and the /t/<token> URL, --strict-mcp-config, no headers anywhere, per-tool allowlist of 117 mcp__<server>__<tool> entries built from a live tools/list of each endpoint (kanban 16, image 15, bank-statement 15, time-tracker 14, expense-tracker 14), --output-format stream-json --verbose --max-turns 20, one --session-id then five --resume per lane. The kanban lane had kanban + time-tracker registered and the bank lane bank-statement + expense-tracker, the way the audits' Part 2 did, so the cross-server choice was live. The image lane was re-run alone in an empty working directory with the CLI's own filesystem tools disallowed, after the first attempt read the real disk instead of uploading. Tool-call counts exclude the client's ToolSearch schema lookups. Machine day 2026-09-04, a Friday.
rubric: 3 = correct, right numbers, no clarification. 2 = correct but needed a second turn, a workaround, or left the user a gap to close. 1 = partially wrong, or asked for something the tool could infer. 0 = failed.

scenarios.prompt: Plan my week for Nova: API design (3h, due Wednesday), docs (2h, Friday), client call prep (1h, Tuesday).
scenarios.note: Board created and all three tasks stored. The deduction is 'Friday': today IS a Friday and the server's D-K6 weekday rule resolves a bare weekday to the nearest day on or after today, so Docs landed on 2026-09-04 while Tuesday and Wednesday rolled to next week. The model noticed the inconsistency itself and spent a fourth call, task_update {due: 2026-09-11}, to fix it. Verified from the endpoint afterwards: NOVA-3 2026-09-08, NOVA-1 2026-09-09, NOVA-2 2026-09-11.
One call, three rows, right columns and dates, 6h total. No invented state.

scenarios.prompt: Start working on the API design.
scenarios.note: task_move NOVA-1 -> doing, then task_start_timer printed the exact time-tracker arguments and the model called mcp__time-tracker__timer_start with them verbatim, across two hosted endpoints on one token. The hosted kanban cannot read the sibling time-tracker store, so the project-name warning is unavailable (documented) - the handoff still spelled the project the same on both sides.

scenarios.prompt: Stop, that took 90 minutes, and mark it done.
scenarios.note: The live timer had run 11 s; the model stopped it, corrected entry c047bed8 to 90 minutes, logged 90 to NOVA-1 and closed it. Both stores verified from the endpoints: time-tracker 1.50 h on Nova / API design, kanban NOVA-1 done with estimate 3h actual 1h 30m.

scenarios.note: Right answer - nothing - and the reasoning is right: NOVA-3 is due Sep 8 and NOVA-2 Sep 11, both after Monday Sep 7, and NOVA-1 is done. It reached it with task_list {due_before: 'next Monday'} rather than overdue {as_of}; the phrase resolved server-side either way, which is the D-K6 fix.

Week 2026-W36, Nova: 1 completed, estimate 3h against actual 1h 30m, the server's own '1h 30m under' line relayed, and the model said unprompted that the two tasks due Sep 8 and Sep 11 fall in W37 and are correctly outside these numbers.

scenarios.prompt: Here is a photo of mine pasted as base64. Save it as "photo", then make a web version 120 px wide and under 3 KB.
scenarios.note: image_upload accepted the pasted base64 and named it photo.jpg (JPEG, 2574 bytes, format from magic bytes). One image_compress with max_width 120 and max_bytes 3000 hit the target in a single encode - the D-I11 fix - and the answer carried the download link. Verified by GET: 200, image/jpeg, filename photo_web.jpg, 2377 bytes, ffd8ffe0, decodes 120x90.

scenarios.prompt: Here is my logo as base64. Save it as "logo", then convert it to JPEG on a white background.
scenarios.note: One convert; the tool flattened the alpha onto white by itself and said so. Verified by GET and decode: image/jpeg, logo.jpg, 2411 bytes, 64x64, and pixel (2,2) - transparent in the source PNG - is rgba(255,255,255,255).

scenarios.prompt: Here is my avatar as base64. Save it as "avatar", then crop it to a centered square and make 32 and 48 px thumbnails.
scenarios.note: image_info showed 96x96, so the model said the centered crop is a no-op rather than pretending to crop, and produced both sizes as two separate download links. Verified: avatar_32.png 200, image/png, 202 bytes, 89504e47, decodes 32x32. The local audit's stray-file deduction cannot happen here - every output is its own link, not a name in a shared directory.

scenarios.prompt: Strip the metadata from the photo.
scenarios.note: One call, no upsell and no size refusal - the D-I8 fix holds on the hosted endpoint - and the re-encode caveat was relayed. Verified: 200, image/jpeg, photo_clean.jpg, 3831 bytes, 0 occurrences of 'exif'. The fixture carried no EXIF payload, so this proves the tool runs and writes, not that a payload was removed.

scenarios.prompt: What are the dominant colours of the logo?
scenarios.note: Three measured colours relayed exactly - #e8b23a 45.1%, #5b3e8a 44.8%, #75537b 0.5% - with the free three-colour cap named and nothing invented. The two named colours are the two the fixture was drawn with, and the shares match their areas (gold ring 29^2-20^2 against purple disc 20^2).

scenarios.prompt: Batch resize all three images to 400 px wide.
scenarios.note: One call, three download links, and the server's own ENLARGED note on each of the three - the D-I4 fix - relayed. This is the case Extension 5 fixed at the shim: the batch tools print the full path so the worker can substitute the download URL, and all three links were present and live. Verified: photo-400x300.jpg 200, image/jpeg, 11660 bytes, decodes 400x300.

scenarios.prompt: Here is my Revolut export. Import it as Main.
scenarios.note: bank_upload stored revolut-main.csv (4295 bytes, 43 lines) and statement_import read it by name: 41 imported, the one REVERTED line dropped and named in the answer, Revolut profile detected, 0 duplicates. Verified from the endpoint: statement_summary for August returns EUR 1283.73 out and EUR 4524.99 in over 36 rows, which is exactly what a csv.DictReader over the source file computes.

scenarios.prompt: Categorise Spotify and Adobe as Software, coffee as Meals.
scenarios.note: The store is right - 3 rules, 12 transactions categorised, 5 Software and 7 Meals, the exact rows the CSV holds. The deduction is a wrong number in the answer: 'three rules set (2 used of the 5 free-tier slots remaining)'. The read path of category_rules returns free_limit 5 and the write path returned only {rules, categorised}, so the model had nothing to read and guessed. D-R52, fixed this round.

scenarios.prompt: What did I spend in August by category?
scenarios.note: The BANK_AUDIT s3 failure (D-B4) did not reproduce. With both servers connected the model went straight to statement_summary {group_by: category} and answered EUR 1283.73 over 36 rows - uncategorised 1129.44, Software 132.99, Meals 21.30 - every figure matching the independent CSV computation, and it separated the EUR 4524.99 money in from spend rather than netting it. It never fell back to the one seeded receipt in the expense ledger.

recurring_detect is Pro; the refusal carried both prices and both tenant-carrying links and the model declined to buy. It then hand-computed the answer from transactions_list and reproduced the exact defect the D-B6 fix removed: Adobe 'every ~2 weeks' annualised from two charges to about EUR 1,656/year. Spotify (three charges, monthly, EUR 119.88/yr) is right. D-R55: the cadence guardrail is behind the paywall, so the free tier gets the unguarded answer instead of no answer.

scenarios.prompt: Which of my expenses have no bank line, and which bank lines have no receipt?
scenarios.note: reconcile_expenses is Pro and refused, so the model reconciled by hand across the two hosted endpoints on the same token: 0 expenses without a bank line (the Adobe EUR 61.50 receipt matches the 08-07 debit exactly), 35 of 36 in-window bank lines without a receipt, and it named the second Adobe charge on 08-21 as the interesting one. It also named the window it could not check, because the expense-tracker free tier returns only the last 30 days. Right answer, entirely by workaround.

scenarios.prompt: Export September to a file I can download.
scenarios.note: statement_export is Pro. Unlike the local audit's s6, the model did not ask which server or which year: it called the right tool with the right range, relayed the refusal with the tenant-carrying link, and then printed the four September rows inline as CSV - 09-01 Spotify 9.99, 09-01 Biedronka 25.00, 09-02 Costa 3.60, 09-03 Zabka 6.40, total 45.09, which is exactly what the source file holds. No file, because the download path is Pro.

totals.note: Not comparable to r10's 19/24, which scored six different endpoints on eight different scenarios. Against the LOCAL Part 2 runs of the same prompts: kanban 17/18 hosted against 18/18 local, image 18/18 hosted against 13/18 as-shipped and 16/18 after the audit fixes, bank-statement 14/18 hosted against 12/18 as-shipped and 13/18 after. Four of the five deductions are the free-tier paywall, not a wrong computation: three bank-statement tools are Pro, and when the tool refuses the model answers anyway, without the tool's guardrails.

defects.title: the upload tools advertise a ceiling the client cannot reach, because the whole payload has to be re-emitted by the model as a tool argument
defects.repro: image_upload's description says the 256 KB body cap is 'about 190 KB of image once base64-encoded'. Pasting a 38,295-byte JPEG (51,061 bytes of base64) into the prompt: the model chose image_upload, then produced no call for 759 s and was still emitting when killed at 15 minutes. The same lane with a 2,574-byte JPEG (3,433 bytes of base64) uploaded in one turn. bank_upload's 4,295-byte CSV took 33 s end to end.
defects.fix: both descriptions now name the binding limit, which is the model's own output, not the request body: image_upload says to keep a paste to roughly 20 KB of base64 (about 15 KB of image) and to shrink the file or run over stdio otherwise; bank_upload says a few KB is quick, tens of KB is a long tool call and 50 KB or more can stall the turn before the upload is sent, and to split a big export by month.

defects.title: category_rules reported the free rule limit when reading and not when writing, so a model that had just written rules guessed how many slots were left, and guessed wrong
defects.repro: category_rules {} -> {count: 0, rules: [], free_limit: 5}; category_rules {rules: [3 rules]} -> {rules: 3, categorised: 12}. The model relayed 'three rules set (2 used of the 5 free-tier slots remaining)'.
defects.fix: the write path now returns free_limit and rules_remaining on the free tier, the same numbers the read path already reported; both are omitted on Pro. Test: servers/bank-statement/test/adversarial.test.mjs 'D-R52: writing rules reports the free limit and what is left, like the read path does'.

defects.title: the 429 named a number and nothing else: no reset time, no upgrade link, and a flat one-hour retry-after on a counter that resets at the top of the UTC hour
defects.repro: the free tier is 600 calls per hour per token and a CLI session re-handshakes every registered endpoint on every turn, so eighteen prompts over five endpoints plus one stalled run exhausted it. Body: {error: rate_limited, limit: 600, window: '1 hour', guide}. retry-after: 3600 at 02:46 UTC, when the bucket actually reset at 03:00. Every other cap on this worker names the price and links to checkout with the tenant attached; this one did not, and it is the cap a real session hits first.
defects.fix: rateLimit() now returns resets_at and retry_after_seconds computed from the hour bucket (655 s, not 3600, in the live repro), a note naming the free ceiling, the Pro ceiling of 6000/hour and the per-turn handshake cost, and upgradeUrl / bundleUrl carrying ?tenant=<anon token>, omitted for a Pro token. The retry-after header carries the real number.

defects.title: statement_import reports date_order 'dmy' with date_order_inferred false for an unambiguous ISO column
defects.repro: a Revolut export whose Completed Date is '2026-08-07 10:00:00' imports correctly - August bucketing is exact against the source file - but the response says date_order 'dmy' and date_order_inferred false, which reads as a decision the parser made and would be wrong if believed. Fix direction: report 'iso' (or 'unambiguous') when every sampled value is YYYY-MM-DD, and reserve dmy/mdy for the case where a choice was actually made.

defects.title: the free tier removes the guardrail rather than the answer: with recurring_detect behind Pro, the model hand-rolls cadence detection and reproduces the exact defect the D-B6 fix closed
defects.repro: b4. recurring_detect refused (Pro). The model computed from transactions_list and reported Adobe as 'every ~2 weeks' with a EUR 1,656/year figure off two charges 14 days apart - the number D-B6 taught the tool to withhold until a third charge, with cadence_confirmed false. Fix direction: let a gated tool answer with its own guardrails and gate the volume or the export instead, or have the refusal state the rule it would have applied ('a cadence is not called until a third charge') so the model that answers anyway inherits it.

defects.title: the hosted kanban cannot read the sibling time-tracker store, so task_start_timer's project-name warning is unavailable
defects.repro: documented in docs/REMOTE_RESULT.md Extension 5. Measured this round in k3: the handoff itself worked and the model passed the printed project name through verbatim, so no misfiling occurred. Recorded as a confirmed-benign seam rather than a live failure; bank-statement's sharedDoc mechanism is the fix if the warning is ever wanted.

client_side.note: The image lane had to be re-run. On the first attempt, in a working directory that held the real fixture files, the model answered 'save it as photo' by shelling out - ls, shasum, Read - decided the local photo.jpg was a different image, and refused to upload rather than calling image_upload at all. Re-run in an empty directory with Bash/Read/Write disallowed, it uploaded immediately. Even then it spent four ToolSearch calls hunting for Write, Bash and PowerShell before accepting that the hosted endpoint IS the filesystem. Not fixable server-side; image_upload's description already opens with 'There is no filesystem here'.
